config.title: useMemo for Expensive Computation

intro.title: useMemo for Expensive Computation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that calculates and displays the factorial of a number. You'll learn how to use the useMemo hook to optimize expensive calculations by caching their results. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the useMemo hook from React's Hooks API. This will help you understand when and how to improve performance in your components by preventing unnecessary recalculations.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, useMemo is essential for optimizing expensive calculations that would otherwise slow down the UI on every render. For example, in a financial dashboard, useMemo can cache complex computations like portfolio performance metrics or risk analysis charts, ensuring smooth interactions when users filter data. Similarly, in e-commerce product filters, it can memoize sorting and filtering logic for large catalogs, preventing lag as customers adjust price ranges or categories. This pattern is also valuable in data visualization tools, where recalculating chart data from large datasets can be deferred until dependencies actually change, maintaining a responsive user experience.

objectives: Implement a React component that performs an expensive calculation without optimization
Apply the useMemo hook to memoize the result of an expensive computation
Configure useMemo dependencies to control when the calculation re-executes
Initialize state variables that trigger expensive recalculations when updated
Manipulate component behavior to demonstrate performance differences with and without memoization
Construct a user interface that displays both the memoized result and the calculation count
Integrate useMemo with TypeScript by properly typing the memoized value and dependencies
